subject: QBR peelback: roadmap commitments audit, launch exposure, and decision asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR peelback: roadmap commitments audit, launch exposure, and decision asks

Team —

Ahead of Friday’s QBR readout I did a quick audit of the top product/eng commitments we promised for HY2 launches and flagged the ones with immediate decision needs. High level: we still have a plausible launch path for the new inference routing feature, but three areas require leadership tradeoffs this week if we want to keep the original GTM window.

Summary (detailed runbook attached):
- Green: Model catalog gating and basic API work — on schedule (engineering has a 2-week buffer).
- Amber: KV cache sharding for Dedicated — perf regressions in long-tail latency surfaced in the integration tests; remediation ETA ~3w unless we scope back release.
- Red: VPC private control-plane telemetry (audit logs)—security review raised two policy-blocking findings that require either engineering changes or an SLA carveout.

Immediate asks:
1) Vivek: we need a decision on sharding scope — invest 3w to keep full behavior or ship a reduced config that preserves 90% perf with fewer edge cases. Impact: full ship +3w; reduced ship = minor feature gap vs roadmap.
2) Monica: confirm whether we can accept the proposed SLA carveout for private telemetry (customer-facing note + legal sign-off) or whether we must re-architect before launch.
3) Please review the attached runbook (QBR_runbook_v2.pdf) and the Gantt (timeline_gantt_v3.xlsx) — I annotated critical path tasks.

Notes on customer risk: Acme is in scope for the initial pilot; I copied their PM (Kate) to keep alignment. If we delay the KV sharding fix, their internal latency budget may force them to pause onboarding.

If you both agree, I’ll prepare a 5-slide decision brief for Friday covering the tradeoffs and recommended asks.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_runbook_v2.pdf (36 pages, runbook), timeline_gantt_v3.xlsx (Gantt, filtered by critical path)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR peelback: roadmap commitments audit, launch exposure, and decision asks

Thanks Hannah — good breakdown. Two quick thoughts:

1) KV sharding: I want a tighter run-estimate from infra before we decide. Monica, can your team give a 48-hour ops-level assessment (risk list + rollback plan) so we know whether the 3w remediation is conservative? If it is, we can likely absorb. If not, we need to prepare the reduced-config messaging.

2) Telemetry/SLA carveout: I prefer avoiding carveouts for initial pilots unless absolutely necessary. Monica, if legal can sign the carveout quickly and we document the mitigations for customers, I’ll consider it — otherwise we gate.

I’ll block 30 minutes tomorrow with both of you to run the decision matrix and finalize the 5-slide brief for Friday.

Vivek
VP, Engineering

Looping in specifics —

VKV sharding (infra assessment):
- Initial triage: the long-tail latency is triggered by shard imbalance under mixed-request distributions.
- Short remediation (reduced scope): implement a fallback single-shard mode and accept a 7–12% higher p95 in worst-case queries. Dev effort: ~5 engineer-weeks (can be staged); Delivery ETA for reduced-scope: 1 week to ship fallback + 1 week to validate. Full fix ETA: 3.5 weeks with additional ops testing.
- Rollback: fallback mode can be toggled by config and rolled back instantly.

Telemetry/SLA carveout:
- Legal has provided a preliminary carveout template but flagged audit-log retention and key-access policy as sensitive. If we proceed with carveout, Acme must accept a 90-day retention policy and a limited-read key escrow. Otherwise we must rework the control plane (~3–4 weeks).

Customer impact: Kate — if we leave the reduced KV sharding fallback active, your pilot latency will likely stay within your current SLA for 90% of traffic but we expect spikes under synthetic stress. If that’s acceptable for your pilot, we can proceed and prioritize the full fix for GA. If not, we should delay the pilot until post-fix.

Actionable asks:
- Vivek: confirm whether we take the staged path (ship fallback, monitor with Acme, and commit to full fix before GA).
- Kate: quick call today to confirm pilot acceptance criteria (15–20 min).

Monica
Sr. Director, Product Operations (acting for Platform)
Redwood Inference

Thanks both — quick recap and recommended path for the QBR slide deck (I’ll circulate the 5-slide brief by 10:00 PDT tomorrow):

Decision paper (recommended):
- Ship with staged fallback for KV sharding: fallback toggled by config, immediate rollback available. Communicate to pilot customers (Acme) that production GA will include the full sharding fix within 8 weeks.
- Accept a time-limited SLA carveout for the private control-plane telemetry for pilots only (90-day retention + escrow conditions). Legal will publish carveout language; we’ll include mitigations and a committed re-architecture timeline for GA.

Why: preserves momentum on sales and pilot onboarding, reduces immediate risk of losing Acme pilot, and gives engineering clear runway for the full fix.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Monica: finalize ops assessment doc and the customer-impact CSV by EOD today. (Monica)
- Legal: circulate carveout language and required customer-facing FAQ by EOD tomorrow. (assigned in internal tracker)
- Hannah: finalize 5-slide decision brief and QBR talking points by 10:00 PDT tomorrow. (Hannah)
- Vivek: approve staged path or escalate to execs by 11:00 PDT tomorrow. (Vivek)

Kate — appreciate your quick feedback this afternoon. If the pilot acceptance criteria below look correct, we’ll move forward with the staged approach and lock a customer review cadence (weekly telemetry sync).

Proposed pilot acceptance criteria (for Acme):
- p95 latency within 1.25x of baseline for 95% of real traffic (excluding synthetic stress tests)
- No data-exfiltration vectors introduced by the temporary carveout
- Weekly telemetry sync and immediate rollback procedure agreed

Thanks —
Hannah
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
